result_text:
The per-rep purchase-order report now leaves cancelled orders out, so the January example gives Anna 1 and Bob 1 (the 2 and 1 in your example count the full set of orders; the new test uses a smaller one).

**Change**
- `src/main/java/com/acme/backoffice/PurchaseOrderStore.java`, `countPerSalesRep`: the count subquery now adds `AND po.status <> 'CANCELLED'` (the existing `NOT_CANCELLED` constant), the same filter the per-quarter and per-weekday counts use. I also updated its Javadoc to say cancelled orders are not counted.
- `src/test/java/com/acme/backoffice/SalesRepPurchaseOrderCountTest.java`: added `leavesCancelledPurchaseOrdersOut`, which has one cancelled order in the period and expects each rep to count only their non-cancelled order. The existing tests had no cancelled case, which is why this went unnoticed.

**Verification**
- `SalesRepPurchaseOrderCountTest` passes (4 tests).
- The other purchase-order test classes (quarter, latest, country, weekday, search, and so on) also passed in an earlier run, before I added the new test. I did not re-run them after the final edit.

Nothing is committed.
